title: System Voltage Fault 0560 (v5)
shortDescription: P0560 flagged for system / battery voltage out of normal operating window.
fullDescription: P0560 flagged for system / battery voltage out of normal operating window. The PCM monitors B+ at the battery sense input; voltage too high indicates regulator overcharge, voltage too low indicates load-dump, weak alternator, or corroded cabling.
safetyImpact: Overvoltage can boil the battery and damage modules; undervoltage can cause sudden module reset while driving.

causes.cause: Corroded battery terminals or ground strap
Worn alternator belt slipping under load

fixSteps.title: Battery + alternator load test
fixSteps.instruction: Test battery state of charge, CCA, and alternator output at idle and 2000 RPM with full electrical load.

fixSteps.title: Check ground straps
fixSteps.instruction: Voltage-drop battery negative to engine and engine to chassis. Should be under 0.1V at full load.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cable terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean B+ and B- terminals. Hidden corrosion under the lead is a frequent cause.

fixSteps.title: Verify PCM B+ sense
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe PCM battery sense pin and compare to actual battery voltage. Difference > 0.3V indicates wiring issue to PCM.

faq.q: Can a bad battery cause this even with a new alternator?
faq.a: Yes - a battery with high internal resistance can drag system voltage down and trigger this code despite a healthy alternator.

faq.q: Why did multiple modules set codes at once?
faq.a: Out-of-range B+ disturbs every module on the bus - clear historical codes after the charging system is repaired.

title: Brake Force Sensor Circuit Fault (C0561) (EXT)
shortDescription: C0561 flagged in the chassis brake force / pedal-feel monitoring circuit.
fullDescription: C0561 flagged in the chassis brake force / pedal-feel monitoring circuit. ABS / EBCM uses brake-pressure or brake-pedal-force sensors to modulate ABS, traction, stability and brake-assist functions; faults disable those systems and may extend stopping distance.
safetyImpact: ABS, traction control and brake assist are typically disabled when this code is active. Drive with extra following distance until repaired.

causes.cause: Wiring chafe at chassis-to-master cylinder harness

fixSteps.title: Capture freeze-frame
fixSteps.instruction: Read freeze-frame data at code set; note pedal force, pressure and vehicle speed. Helps identify intermittent vs hard fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check the brake-force sensor connector for water intrusion, bent pins, and chafe.

fixSteps.title: Bench-test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With brake-pedal-force sweep, sensor output should change linearly. A flat or stepped output indicates failed sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace and recalibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Replace sensor; many platforms require EBCM bleed and yaw/steering recalibration after.
tools: scan tool with chassis service mode

faq.q: Is the car safe to drive?
faq.a: Base hydraulic braking still works, but ABS and stability control are disabled. Drive cautiously and avoid hard braking until repaired.

faq.q: Will this clear by itself?
faq.a: If it is a wiring intermittent it may go pending, but the EBCM stores the history; a scan-tool clear is usually required.

fullDescription: C0566 flagged in the chassis brake force / pedal-feel monitoring circuit. ABS / EBCM uses brake-pressure or brake-pedal-force sensors to modulate ABS, traction, stability and brake-assist functions; faults disable those systems and may extend stopping distance.
safetyImpact: ABS, traction control and brake assist are typically disabled when this code is active. Drive with extra following distance until repaired.

causes.cause: Wiring chafe at chassis-to-master cylinder harness

fixSteps.title: Capture freeze-frame
fixSteps.instruction: Read freeze-frame data at code set; note pedal force, pressure and vehicle speed. Helps identify intermittent vs hard fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check the brake-force sensor connector for water intrusion, bent pins, and chafe.

fixSteps.title: Bench-test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With brake-pedal-force sweep, sensor output should change linearly. A flat or stepped output indicates failed sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace and recalibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Replace sensor; many platforms require EBCM bleed and yaw/steering recalibration after.
tools: scan tool with chassis service mode

faq.q: Is the car safe to drive?
faq.a: Base hydraulic braking still works, but ABS and stability control are disabled. Drive cautiously and avoid hard braking until repaired.

faq.q: Will this clear by itself?
faq.a: If it is a wiring intermittent it may go pending, but the EBCM stores the history; a scan-tool clear is usually required.

title: Steering / EPS Variant Fault (P1700) (EXT)
shortDescription: P1700 flagged by the EPS / steering control module for a torque, position or motor feedback fault.
fullDescription: P1700 flagged by the EPS / steering control module for a torque, position or motor feedback fault. EPS uses torque sensors at the column and motor-position sensors at the rack; either side out of plausibility disables assist and sets a chassis code.
safetyImpact: Loss of power steering assist increases steering effort dramatically, especially at parking speeds.

causes.cause: CAN bus fault to EPS module

fixSteps.title: Battery and grounds
fixSteps.instruction: EPS is sensitive to low B+ - test battery and module ground at the EPS connector.

fixSteps.title: Read EPS-specific data
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool that supports EPS module to view torque-sensor, motor current and angle data live.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate steering angle
fixSteps.instruction: After alignment or battery work, perform steering-angle relearn; often clears spurious EPS codes.
tools: scan tool with chassis service mode

fixSteps.title: Replace EPS unit
fixSteps.instruction: If torque sensor or motor is internally failed, the column or rack assembly is replaced as a unit on most platforms.

faq.q: Can I drive without power steering?
faq.a: Yes, but parking and low-speed maneuvers will require much more effort. Avoid traffic until repaired.

faq.q: Does it always require a new rack?
faq.a: Not always - calibration, low B+ and connector issues are repaired far more often than the rack itself.
